subject: SIG access artifacts request — SafeBank (SAML / SCIM / RBAC)
messages:
From: Alice Sullivan <alice.sullivan@safebank.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procuresec@safebank.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Access artifacts for SIG assessment - SafeBank

Hi Tessa,

We are starting the SIG intake for our upcoming vendor review and need a consolidated bundle of access control evidence. To scope: SafeBank requires artifacts covering SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, and role/entitlement mapping (RBAC) for the tenant that will be in-scope. Specifically we need:

- SAML assertion samples (both successful and failed flows) covering the past 90 days, with timestamps and NameID placeholders redacted as needed.
- SCIM delta export for the last 30 days (CSV preferred).
- Current RBAC matrix (roles -> example entitlements) and a short narrative describing how least-privilege is enforced for service accounts and cross-tenant roles.
- A signed least-privilege attestation from the product/security owner (PDF).

Can you confirm: 1) whether you can deliver a single zipped bundle, 2) an estimated delivery date (SafeBank requests within 10 business days), and 3) any PII/PHI we should expect to redact? We have a DocuSign request to attach the attestation once you confirm the signer.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Regards,
Alice Sullivan
Senior Vendor Risk Analyst
SafeBank Vendor Risk Management
alice.sullivan@safebank.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Sullivan <alice.sullivan@safebank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Access artifacts for SIG assessment - SafeBank

On Wed, 30 Sep 2026 at 09:12 AM Alice Sullivan <alice.sullivan@safebank.com> wrote:
> We are starting the SIG intake for our upcoming vendor review and need a consolidated bundle of access control evidence.
> Specifically we need SAML samples, SCIM delta, RBAC matrix, and a signed attestation.

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We can produce the bundle. Proposed owners and plan: 

- Marissa Cole (security operations) will pull SAML assertion samples and the SCIM delta extraction. She will flag any assertion logs that contain PII for redaction.
- Sean Gallagher (customer success/onboarding) will extract the RBAC matrix and provide the role->entitlement mapping plus the short narrative on least-privilege enforcement.
- I will coordinate the least-privilege attestation PDF and set up the DocuSign once you confirm the signer.

Timeline: target delivery in 8 business days (2026-10-12) to give the team time to sample and redact; we can accelerate to 6 business days if we treat the attestation as a later follow-up. If you need 10 calendar days instead of business days, confirm and we'll aim for 2026-10-10.

Redaction note: our default is to redact user identifiers (NameID/email) and replace with stable placeholders; timestamps and assertion IDs are provided. If SafeBank needs raw timestamps for correlation, call that out and we can provide a redaction map under an NDA addendum.

Do you prefer one zipped bundle or separate deliverables? Also: can you share the HubSpot SR# or the SIG questionnaire link so we can attach deliverables to the intake?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Compliance Partnerships
Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0144

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: Alice Sullivan <alice.sullivan@safebank.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Access artifacts for SIG assessment - SafeBank

Tessa / Sean / Alice — delivering the initial artifact bundle for review. See attachments and the Drive folder link for full files. Notes below.

Attachments (zipped bundle delivered via Drive):
- saml-assertion-samples.tar.gz (contains 30 sampled assertions: 25 successes, 5 failed). Fields with direct PII have been replaced with placeholders like <REDACTED_EMAIL>.
- scim-delta-snapshot.csv (30-day delta export; includes UTC timestamps and operation type).
- rbac-mapping-v2.xlsx (role definitions + example entitlements + owner column).
- least-privilege-attestation-draft.pdf (unsigned draft from product).

Redaction and sampling methodology: we sampled by transaction id across peak and off-peak windows to capture different auth flows. We excluded raw authentication tokens and replaced real email addresses. Assertion timestamps are intact. We flagged two failed assertions tied to transient federation errors — those are included as 'failed_flow_1' and 'failed_flow_2' in the archive.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_safebank_evidence (folder has checksums and a redaction index).

Next steps I propose:
1) Tessa to approve the attestation signer and trigger DocuSign.
2) Sean to add a short paragraph to the RBAC sheet describing JIT provisioning and service-account boundaries.
3) We wait for SafeBank feedback on sampling/redaction — they may request additional raw timestamps.

Happy to schedule a 20-min sync if SafeBank wants to walk the artifacts.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — I confirm receipt of the Drive bundle and attachments. A few follow-ups: 

1) The sampling looks reasonable; we do need assertion timestamps for two specific failed flows for correlation with our logs. If you can provide a redaction map (ID->placeholder) for those two failed assertions, that will be sufficient.
2) Please have the least-privilege attestation signed and returned via DocuSign by end of day 2026-10-06. Our legal team requires a signature on company letterhead.
3) Sean, can you expand the RBAC narrative to include any delegated admin roles and how they are restricted? A short paragraph will do.

We prefer a single zipped bundle (Drive folder is fine). HubSpot SR#: 98765 — please attach the Drive link to that record.

If anything blocks the 10/06 attestation timeline, let me know today and we can arrange an SLA exception window. Otherwise this looks good, thank you.

Regards,
Alice Sullivan
